articles.title: AI Increases ARPU for Indian Job Search Platform
articles.content: While AI dented traffic and billings for Shiksha for the second consecutive quarter in Q1 FY27, it emerged as a new monetisation lever for Naukri, Info Edge’s recruitment business. “Newer monetisation levers such as AI REX, Talent Pulse, and other value-added offerings contributed to significantly higher ARPU and expanded our revenue opportunity per customer,” said Hitesh Oberoi, Info Edge’s managing director, during the earnings call . The management highlighted that commercial adoption of AI REX, the company’s agentic AI offering for recruiters, continued to accelerate during the quarter. As of June 2026, AI REX was live across 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms, 10% of which have already converted into paying customers. Adoption of AI REX spans across sectors such as IT, BFSI, sales, finance, healthcare, BPO and core engineering. The company said it sold AI REX to 400 clients in Q1 FY27 and another 300 clients in July. This was achieved by increasing talent demand across AI, machine learning, data science and data engineering. Talent Pulse, the firm’s AI-powered talent and salary intelligence platform, now serves more than 600 paid customers, ranging from large enterprises to smaller organisations. Early traction has prompted the company to scale both AI REX and Talent Pulse to several thousand customers over the next few quarters. Naukri is diversifying beyond a jobs platform. The management highlighted that Naukri is transitioning from just being a jobs board into a more comprehensive recruitment operating system. The platform now spans sourcing solutions across the premium mid-market and value segments, salary and talent planning tools, AI-led recruiter productivity capabilities, employer branding, assisted hiring services, and assessments. “Our growth strategy is built around hiring volumes, our share of hiring, and our revenue per hire. Hiring volumes depend on the broader microeconomic environment, so our focus remains on expanding market share and revenue per hire,” Oberoi told analysts on the call. In the premium segment, the platform continues to expand its presence through Naukri TopTier, PremiumX, IIM Jobs and Hirist. The company believes it has not fully tapped the monetisation potential across these offerings, as several features are currently being offered to customers at no additional cost. In the mid-market segment, Naukri is aiming to boost recruiter productivity through AI-led sourcing automation, while expanding adjacent offerings such as job marketing, talent intelligence, data products, and assisted hiring services. JobHai remains a medium-term strategic opportunity in the value segment. On the job seeker side, Naukri is evolving from job search and discovery towards broader offerings including career insights, personalised advice, upskilling and interview preparation through Naukri 360, Naukri Minis. It also has AI-powered agents such as NEO. “These self-serve AI-enabled offerings typically carry high margins, and the acquisition of node Coding Ninja should help us expand further into upskilling. We believe this is a meaningful opportunity enabled by our AI capabilities and data assets,” Oberoi said. The jobseeker business, Naukri 360, saw billings grow by over 35% YoY in Q1 FY27. Over the last six quarters, paid subscribers as a percentage of monthly active users have improved from 1.3% to 2.6%, aided by increased adoption of AI initiatives, including Jobseeker agent NEO, AI mock interview offerings and AI Resume Builder offerings. Naukri operates on a massive scale. The platform contains about 118 million resumes, with over 25,000 new profiles being added every day. Alongside that 850,000 daily profile modifications and millions of other behavioural interactions also happen across the platform. These data assets remain one of its biggest competitive advantages. AI does not pose disintermediation risk to Naukri: The management commentary also noted AI disintermediation risk as being inconsequential to Naukri, given the company’s control over its proprietary data on both sides of the marketplace. “We have proprietary data from both sides of the marketplace, millions of user interactions every day, and over two decades of domain knowledge. We believe these strengths become even more valuable in an AI-driven world,” said Oberoi. However, Shiksha, the education arm of Info Edge, faces a different challenge as a large part of user traffic came through a distribution channel it did not own. As AI changed search behaviour, that dependency became a disadvantage. “Where we own both sides of the marketplace, AI strengthens the business by improving matching recommendations and customer outcomes. Where we rely more on third-party distribution, AI-driven changes in user discovery and search behaviour created headwinds for the business. This is how we think about AI risk across our portfolio, said Oberoi. articles.title: Trump Offered Early Access to Truth Social
articles.content: Over 10 customers have signed up for Truth Social’s new Truth API program, which offers paid subscribers the “fastest” access to posts in real-time, within the first two weeks of the product’s launch. APIs, or application programming interfaces, allow firms and businesses that would benefit from early access to influential social media posts to have licensed, real-time access to posts through a subscription-based data feed. Many major social media platforms, such as Instagram and X, offer APIs to interested customers. However, only Truth Social is home to President Donald Trump’s breaking news announcements on market-moving topics. Recommended Stories FCC removes TV broadcasters’ market share cap, opening the way for bigger mergers South Korean police raid Starbucks headquarters over ‘Tank Day’ campaign Mamdani purges dozens of corporate leaders from city-backed nonprofit organization Trump Media and Technology Group announced its new Truth API in mid-July, allowing customers early access to important posts, following the product’s launch on Aug. 1 with a $100,000 price tag. Kevin McGurn, the interim chief executive officer of Trump Media, announced that the company received over 10 subscribers to its API program as part of his 2026 second-quarter financial results. Several of these customers were onboarded before the Aug. 1 launch date. “Our new Truth API product is already generating revenue, with more than ten customer agreements signed to date,” McGurn said. “I’m encouraged by this momentum, and shareholders should expect more frequent communication from us on our progress each quarter as we enter this next chapter.” In the company’s Q2 results, Trump Media reported $2 billion in total assets and $1.9 billion in financial assets, while also reporting a $238.1 million net loss for the quarter. It said the bulk of the quarter’s losses were non-cash, including losses on digital assets, or cryptocurrency . Trump Media also reported $1.7 million in revenue for Q2, which is up nearly 90% from the $0.9 million in revenue it reported in Q2 2025. McGurn said the company has “sharpened our strategic direction and brought real discipline to how we allocate capital” in the past several months. The company said it would be looking to cut costs and create a “leaner operating structure” and focus on its “strategic growth initiatives” over the coming months as it looks to save costs. McGurn said in July that the Truth API would be a “high-margin, recurring revenue stream” for Trump Media. Democrats have begun to target the company’s API, citing ethical and conflict-of-interest concerns, as the president has the most followers of any account on the platform, with 13 million as of Tuesday morning. Trump has made major policy decisions about topics ranging from the Iran war to tariffs to executive appointments and announced them first on Truth Social. Mark Warner (D-VA) argued in a letter to the presidents of the Bank Policy Institute, Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association, Managed Funds Association, Financial Services Forum, Principal Traders Group, and American Bankers Association that the API product “creates a clear and unacceptable pathway for corruption.” Trump Media addressed some of the pushback on the product in its second quarter results, saying it believes it has received “factually inaccurate criticism.”

articles.title: EVs Dominate China's Car Market: Key Takeaways
articles.content: LivestreamMenuBYD failed to break the ranks of the three most popular car models sold in China in recent months, according to Autohome data.Tesla held up well, while Volkswagen was the only traditional foreign automaker.In this article BEIJING — Survivors have emerged in China's fiercely competitive car market, which is increasingly dominated by electric-powered vehicles. Here are brands that have emerged as Chinese consumers' favorite, according to industry data from Autohome: Among the 10 most popular car models sold in China in the six months through July, Geely's Xingyuan electric hatchback was the bestseller with nearly 197,500 units sold. Geely has emerged as a close rival to BYD, ranking second by overall China sales volume in 2025. The Hangzhou-based company still sells gasoline-powered cars in addition to electric vehicles, such as those sold under its premium brand Zeekr. The company's Model Y ranked second in popularity with more than 180,000 of the electric SUVs sold. The Tesla car comes at a steeper price tag of 263,500 yuan to 313,500 yuan, but that didn't stop it from topping sales of Li Auto's i6 SUV and Xiaomi's SU7 sedan. Three of the 10 best-selling cars, as per Autohome data from February through July, were from BYD. But the most popular one — a modestly priced Yuan UP SUV — just managed fifth place with nearly 97,700 units sold. In sixth place was the Ti 7 under BYD's off-road brand, followed by its Sealion 06 SUV. The Chinese car giant reported its passenger car sales dropped by more than 10% in the first half of the year. The German automaker was the only traditional foreign car company to make the top 10 — with its compact gasoline-powered Lavida in ninth place, squeezed between Leapmotor's A10 electric SUV and Geely's gasoline-powered Boyue L SUV. New energy vehicles, which include battery and hybrid-powered cars, accounted for 65.1% of new passenger cars sold in July — up from 54% a year ago, according to China Passenger Car Association data released Tuesday. But the category still saw sales for the year through July drop by 12.5%, as passenger car sales overall tumbled by 20.3%, industry data showed.

This dominance has profound implications for the global auto industry, accelerating the shift away from internal combustion engines and intensifying competition among international automakers to capture a share of the world's largest EV market.
